title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. F_A(X) = Hom_1(A,X) is a representable functor on a symmetric monoidal category of modules over k, with ⊗ and unit 1. The previous page shows that making F_A lax monoidal amounts to giving A a counital, coassociative, cocommutative coalgebra structure Δ: A→A⊗A, ε: A→1. That structure makes Hom(A,X) an algebra under the convolution product.

Question. When does Hom(A,X) carry divided powers natural in X, i.e. compatible maps Γ^p F_A(X) → F_A(Γ^p X) making Γ^*F_A(X) → F_A(Γ^*X) a map of ⊗-rings?

Data. By Yoneda (made explicit on the next page), a natural (polynomial) operation f ↦ f^{(p)} from F_A to F_A∘Γ^p is the same as an element u_p ∈ Hom(A, Γ^p A). One then sets f^{(p)} := Γ^p(f)∘u_p : A → Γ^p X.

Mixed products. For f,g: A ⇉ X, f^{(p)}g^{(q)} is defined as the composite
A --Δ--> A⊗A --(Γ^p f∘u_p)⊗(Γ^q g∘u_q)--> Γ^pX⊗Γ^qX --mult--> Γ^{p+q}X,
which is the convolution product in Hom(A, Γ^*X). The page draws the square that must commute: Γ^pF_A(X)⊗Γ^qF_A(X) → F_AΓ^p(X)⊗F_AΓ^q(X) → F_A(Γ^pX⊗Γ^qX) → F_AΓ^{p+q}(X), versus going through Γ^{p+q}F_A(X).

Key axiom. To check f^{(p)}f^{(q)} = c_{pq} f^{(p+q)} with c_{pq} = binom(p+q,p), it suffices to treat the universal case X = A, f = id_A. The condition becomes
mult∘(u_p⊗u_q)∘Δ = c_{pq} u_{p+q} in Hom(A, Γ^{p+q}A).

Conclusion of the page. Γ^*F(A) → F(Γ^*X) is a homomorphism of ⊗-rings 'car F commute à ⊗'.

Next page. The remaining axioms translate likewise:
- u_0 = 1 and u_1 = id;
- (f+g)^{(p)} = Σ f^{(i)}g^{(j)} reduces, via the universal case A×A with Δ = inj_1 + inj_2, to Δ(u_p) = Σ_{i+j=p} u_i⊗u_j.
So the u_p form a 'divided power sequence' A → Γ^*A compatible with the coproducts.

Purpose. This classifies representable functors with values in PD-algebras, i.e. co-PD-algebra objects A. It is presumably meant to put PD structures functorially on Hom/de Rham-type constructions for the divided-power de Rham complex lecture (IHÉS 1976).
errors: The display 'f^{(p)} ∈ Γ^p(F_A X)⊗Γ^q(F_A X) ∋ g^{(q)}' is loose: f^{(p)} lies in Γ^p F_A(X) and g^{(q)} in Γ^q F_A(X).

Γ^p∘F_A is not representable by A. The Yoneda reduction is legitimate for (polynomial) operations F_A → F_A∘Γ^p, and the universal-element argument at X = A, f = id needs naturality in X with respect to all morphisms, which holds. Not an error, but the page does not spell this out.
Cocommutativity of Δ and compatibility of u_p with the counit are needed for commutativity and unit axioms; these are only listed on the previous page.
The constant c_{pq} is left unspecified; it must be the binomial coefficient binom(p+q,p).

ideas.what: Lax monoidal structures on representable functor Hom(A,-) correspond to (cocommutative) coalgebra structures on A; convolution product
ideas.modern_name: Convolution algebra / co-algebra objects representing ring-valued functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Hopf algebra theory; Tall–Wraith 1970 for co-ring objects)

ideas.what: Natural divided-power operations on Hom(A,X) correspond to elements u_p ∈ Hom(A,Γ^pA) with u_0=1, u_1=id, Δ(u_p)=Σu_i⊗u_j and mult(u_p⊗u_q)Δ = binom(p+q,p) u_{p+q}
ideas.modern_name: Co-PD-algebra objects / representing objects for PD-algebra-valued functors (plethory-type structures over Γ, divided power coalgebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (Γ functor, polynomial laws, 1963–65); plethory viewpoint Tall–Wraith, Borger–Wieland (2005)

ideas.what: Reduction of identities to the universal case X=A, f=id_A (or A×A with injections) via Yoneda

missed.claim: The page sketches the classification of divided-power-algebra-valued representable functors on modules by 'co-PD' structures on the representing coalgebra (u_p: A→Γ^pA with coproduct and product compatibilities). This is an analogue of Tall–Wraith/plethory theory for the Γ (divided power) monad. Such divided-power plethory-type objects are only sparsely treated in later literature, but the computation here is routine.
missed.quote: Il suffit de traiter X=Y=A, f=g=id_A ... 1^{(p)}1^{(q)} = c_{pq}1^{(p+q)} ... Γ^*F(A) → F(Γ^*(X)) ⊗-anneau car F commute à ⊗
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Divided-power analogues of plethories (co-PD-ring objects) are relevant to crystalline/de Rham–Witt and derived PD theories, but this page gives only the elementary Yoneda dictionary.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine Yoneda-style translation of divided-power axioms on Hom(A,X) into conditions on elements u_p ∈ Hom(A,Γ^pA). It is correct and mildly anticipates plethory-type thinking for Γ, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'f^{(p)}⊗g^{(p)}' in the image is likely intended as f^{(p)}⊗g^{(q)}.
'Γ^{p+q}F_A(X) — F_AΓ^{p+q}(X)' is a horizontal arrow (comparison map), not a dash.
The struck lower line reads roughly '[-représente id_A^{(p+q)}, dans c_{p,q} id_A^{(p+q)}-]'; the surviving equation is '1^{(p)}1^{(q)} = c_{pq} 1^{(p+q)}'.
'Γ^*F(A) → F(Γ^*(X))' probably should read Γ^*F(X) → F(Γ^*(X)); the A is overwritten in the image.
Bottom line: '⊗-anneau ... ⊗-anneau, car F commute à ⊗'.
